conclusion: No demonstrated material optimization found that preserves all original progress boundaries, complete fresh pathname/boot/current-thread-membership/limits reads and original error priority. Absolute immutable CStr spelling is an implementable small experiment; descriptor-relative shortcuts are not established equivalent.

ordered_observations: fresh boot_id complete text and comparison
fresh current calling-thread cgroup complete text and membership
parse all five only after all five successful reads, then compare expected Limits
per_successful_check.syscall_count_kind: derived from exact source on ordinary nonempty short files, not a measured strace result; EINTR, fragmented reads, fallback or long context can add calls; observer CPU clock calls excluded

allocation_review.remaining_heap_paths: Long context above 256 bytes retains original complete-read fallback; errors may allocate. Resolver and resource_sample have one-time/phase-boundary work, not the 8817-check loop.

safe_small_candidate.name: immutable absolute CStr spellings, fresh same libc open64 each time
safe_small_candidate.production_sketch: Keep the existing parent metadata implementation. Prebuild only immutable absolute path bytes for boot, thread-self membership and five limits. A small open helper must mirror std open64 O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC, mode argument, EINTR handling, owned-fd conversion and exactly one close; pass resulting File through the unchanged read-to-EOF functions and unchanged error mapping.
safe_small_candidate.performance_interpretation: Only short copy/NUL validation and thin user-space wrapper work can be removed. No evidence supports a large speedup or Host gate success.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Held parent directory FD with dev/inode fences
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: A persistent new bind-mount view can retain the same underlying parent dev/inode while different child mounts expose changed limit files. Relative openat continues through the old held mount view; full absolute opens see the new view. Fresh limits relative to an old dirfd are not fresh current absolute-path observations.
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.status: Do not reuse the 630cd5ee mechanism as an established equivalent.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Held or per-check parent FD plus fresh absolute parent statx mount-ID before/after five reads
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: A mount-ID comparison can catch a persistent parent mount replacement at the fence if supported and checked correctly. It does not attest ancestor search permissions during each child read: revoke ancestor execute/ACL permission after the initial fence, perform relative opens, restore before the final fence. Absolute original opens during that interval fail, while relative opens bypass those ancestors. A persistent revocation caught only by the final parent fence can also change the original I/O error ordering/class. The original checker itself is sequential, not an atomic snapshot; adding a blind interval is not equivalent.
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.status: Equivalence unproved; cannot merge as optimization. Closing with a full absolute permission/path traversal per file forfeits the intended prefix-walk saving and adds operations.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Open fresh parent directory once per verify, then openat children
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: It avoids cross-check descriptor reuse but freezes the prefix within the check, so intermediate mount/ancestor permission/name changes still differ from five full absolute opens. It also adds parent open/fstat/close in place of one lstat/statx.
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.status: Unproved, and syscall count can increase.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Omit second read after a short read / stop at newline / use known pseudo-file size
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: Original contract explicitly requires true EOF and retains fragmented reads, EINTR, late I/O failure, complete UTF-8 validation, and 128-byte overflow rejection. A short read is not EOF.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Cache boot ID result, membership FD, limit descriptors/values or manually reuse one TID pathname
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: Misses changed current proc/mount/permission view or a different calling worker. Explicit TID spellings also require proof against procfs PID-namespace changes; /proc/thread-self currently resolves the actual caller afresh.

unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.mechanism: Batch through io_uring or cached-only openat2
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.counterexample: Not an established semantics-preserving reduction: ordered read/parse failures and caller-thread membership must remain exact; async workers may change thread-self resolution, extra workers/resource policy need analysis, and ordinary opens already attempt cached VFS traversal.
unproven_or_rejected_shortcuts.status: No demonstrated benefit or equivalence; not an immediate implementation option.

recommended_measurement_before_changes: Use an isolated candidate; leave frozen d873 and its original four-second tests unchanged. Preserve exact compiler/profile/source/binary identity and measure the baseline and CStr candidate in the same actual fixed Host on each architecture.
First confirm the derived syscall mix with a separate short strace diagnostic. Traced results are for attribution only, not timing/qualification evidence.

Run a separate read-only component ABBA comparison with fixed call counts (at least the observed 8817 checks per sample) and aggregate thread user/system CPU plus wall time. Keep initial resolver work separate from the hot verify loop. Avoid per-file timing instrumentation in the original business qualification run.

Retain all existing complete-read/replacement/EINTR/UTF-8/128-byte/IO-before-parse controls against the actual new helper. Retain current thread membership and real Host revocation controls. Do not discard failed or slower samples.

Only a measured material reduction under those controls justifies implementing it as a performance fix; then rerun the original fixed Host four-second/16-worker independent replay and confirmation gate. Component CPU changes cannot qualify that business gate.

primary_sources.finding: Paths shorter than 384 bytes use MaybeUninit stack storage, copy only the path, append NUL, and validate CStr; they do not allocate a CString.
File opens perform the path conversion, then libc open64 with O_CLOEXEC and EINTR retry. Linux GNU lstat uses statx when available, otherwise lstat64.
An absolute name starts from the current root; a relative dirfd starts from the held file f_path. Ancestor lookup permission checks occur during pathname traversal, not by a mount-ID comparison.

Each normal open allocates and installs a fresh file description after current pathname resolution; the v6.8 source is semantic reference, not a claim about the exact hosted kernel build or performance.
